evidence:
Run order and shared state: tests/test.sh:104-113 launches one app process on one DB; test.sh:213 runs the gates suite and test.sh:224 the scored suite with '--max-concurrent-agent 1' (test.sh:207), so render -> constraints -> functional/polish/visual all hit the same mutated database; functional additionally restarts the process (functional/prompt.md:57 P10). No dimension resets state, so tolerance must come from wording. It does:

(1) Gates. gates/render/prompt.md:9 'Do not mutate economic records'. gates/constraints/judge.toml:26 'Use only your two uniquely named records and leave them in place. Never settle a seeded offer or another judge's record. Every scored suite must tolerate this additional requisition and pending offer.' constraints/prompt.md:9 'Use unique titles/candidates with a session suffix ... do not approve, revise or rescind.' The gate's own assertion is identity-scoped ('Exactly one of each saved identity must be present'), not a collection count.

(2) Functional acknowledges the gate mutation explicitly: functional/prompt.md:17 'Earlier gates may have added a unique requisition and PENDING offer; treat both as existing shared state, never your own controls, and do not revise or rescind them. Use unique identifiers with a short per-session suffix; never mutate another judge's records. Create dedicated requisitions with ample budgets'. It is seed-independent: prompt.md:27 'Operational demonstration rows are optional: create your own controls rather than demanding any imported roster'; prompt.md:47 'No dependence on any seeded requisition's remaining room'; prompt.md:53 'This is the sole permitted seed-operation probe; never intentionally settle seed offers. Omitted operational history remains valid.' Counts are state-relative: prompt.md:23 'Record before/after facts per row and per record ... Actions may add ordinary extra audit entries, so do not demand exact global counts.' Criteria follow suit: hro_commitment (judge.toml:443) 'record its budget, existing movements and headroom, then approve ... Use judge-created records; no imported requisition is required'; hro_draft_eligibility (judge.toml:650) is conditional on seed presence; hro_restart (judge.toml:902) 'Record any imported operational seed IDs/counts ... seed IDs remain exactly once' is read-then-compare; D2/hro_whatif_roles (judge.toml:1361) 'A fresh product read before and after shows no additional saved preview'; the B5 prepare rows (e.g. judge.toml:1181) 'existing legitimate previews remain intact'. All fixed figures (100001.77, 39.75, 0.00->0.00 headrooms, etc.) are on judge-created requisitions with stated budgets, not on seed rows. I found no criterion in functional/judge.toml that quotes a seeded figure, a global collection size or an empty-collection expectation.

(3) Polish (runs after functional's heavy mutation and its restart): polish/prompt.md:11 'Use a dimension-specific ID suffix and leave the record in place'; prompt.md:14 'Use dedicated Polish-owned records. Prepare simple current committed hires by creating as Recruiter and approving ... Other judges' records are not controls.' Every polish criterion builds its own preview on 'dedicated hires' (polish/judge.toml:23, 50) and compares against its own recorded pre-state.

(4) Visual: visual/prompt.md:14 'perform a read-only review ... Do not approve,revise,rescind or depend on another judge's exact data'; prompt.md:12 'empty operational collections are allowed'. Likert anchors (visual/judge.toml) describe craft, not specific rows, so a desk populated by hundreds of functional records is neither required nor penalised.

(5) app_context.md:21 'Operational demonstration rows may be absent; prepare your own controls.'

Broken-app-could-pass probe: an app that re-seeds/wipes on restart cannot hide behind this tolerance, because hro_restart demands the fresh writes survive; nothing in the tolerance wording grants credit for absent state. Conforming-alternative-could-fail probe: see latent items below; neither is a pristine-seed assumption.

Latent items (P3, not exercised by any run):
(a) Operation-key namespace across dimensions. Keys are scoped to the signed-in actor, not to a judge session (hireops_rules.md section 11: 'The key belongs to that signed-in actor and identifies one immutable intent'; golden src/change-sets.js:11 'UNIQUE(actor_id,operation_key)', :105 409 on different intent). Functional and Polish both prepare as the single Finance account. Functional is told to use a per-session suffix (prompt.md:17, :61 'Use distinct operation keys'), but Polish only says 'a distinctive operation key' / 'use a new key' (polish/judge.toml:32, prompt.md:16); its dimension-suffix sentence (prompt.md:11) is attached to the gate requisition ID. The golden pre-fills a random key (public/js/change-sets.js:19,45), so the reference is unaffected; an app with an empty key field relies on the Polish judge not re-typing a key Functional already saved.
(b) Leftover unsent editor entries. hireops_rules.md:544-551 lets the implementer choose where unsent entries live ('Where the entries are kept is yours'). The golden uses localStorage (public/js/change-sets.js:65-77) and every judge.toml launches playwright-mcp with '--isolated', so the golden's later judges start with clean editors. An app that keeps them server-side per user would present Polish's Finance and Recruiter sign-ins with editors already holding Functional's E1/D2/L2 leftovers (possibly flagged 'no longer current'). hro_pol_session_resume is worded relatively ('the editor shows neither that key nor those terms'), so a careful judge still grades correctly, but no Polish sentence says the editor may be pre-populated.

Measurement status: raw-evidence-index.json states 'Full configured grading/workload ... are absent' and its entries are scripted golden observations only (all 10 artifact hashes and the 14 source hashes re-verified by me). live-desk.json does show 'process restart keeps saved changes; retry returns the original receipt; live updates resume after restart' passed for the golden, which supports Polish's live-update row being observable after Functional's restart, but it is a scripted run on a small fixture, not the configured gates->functional->polish->visual sequence on a heavily mutated DB. The in-suite order of functional/polish/visual under rewardkit was not observed. Hence risk=true and run_verdict NOT EXERCISED; the Pass is a source-wording verdict for this row only.
counterexample: No demonstrated failure. Latent only: (a) a conforming app whose operation-key input starts empty; the Polish judge types a 'distinctive' key that the Functional judge already saved as Finance with a different intent -> prepare returns 409 by the public contract -> hro_pol_session_resume ('saving now succeeds') or hro_pol_change_recovery is scored 0 for harness-state reasons. (b) a conforming app storing unsent entries server-side per user; the Polish judge opens Finance's editor pre-filled with Functional's leftover, possibly stale-flagged members and may misattribute them.
suggested_fix: In tests/scored/polish/prompt.md add one sentence: earlier reviews leave saved previews, receipts and possibly unsent editor entries for the same accounts; ignore or overwrite them, and give every operation key a Polish-specific session suffix. Then obtain one full configured verifier run on the golden to observe the sequential suites on the mutated database.
